meta.title: A Day at the Toy Factory

paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. On Monday, Teacher Kim put a notice on the door of our class. It said, "Toy factory visit: Thursday, the twelfth of November. The bus leaves school at nine o'clock. The tour starts at ten o'clock and finishes at noon. Ticket: twenty baht for each child. Wear sneakers." "Why sneakers?" asked Leo. "It is better to walk in sneakers," said Teacher Kim.

On Thursday, we came to the factory at ten o'clock. The ticket office was next to the gate. Teacher Kim gave the woman in the office the money. "Thirty children, twenty baht each," she said. "That is six hundred baht." The woman gave her all the tickets. A sign on the wall said, "Please speak quietly in the factory." We all spoke very quietly.

A woman from the factory showed us a long table with many soft toys. First, a machine cut the white cloth. Then a woman made the cloth into the shape of a snowman. Next, a man put soft wool in the snowman. Mia looked at a snowman with a red hat. "Can we make one?" she asked. "Not today," said the woman, "but you can finish a small one at home."

At noon, the tour finished. At the shop, each child could buy a small toy. Mia chose the snowman with the red hat. It was fifteen baht. We took the bus back to school at one o'clock. In the afternoon, I wrote about the visit. I read the notice again for the dates and the prices. It told me all that I needed to know.
